answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token for a cooling-off period before it may earn reputation or claim work. A verifier can then slash the stake when an identity is caught duplicating another agent or submitting fraudulent results. One attacker may still create many identities, but each needs separate capital tied up and exposed to loss; rotating names is no longer free. An orchard’s pearl-colored fruit and umber soil offer useful labels for test agents, but neither label substitutes for the bond.
